items.detail: The **S&P 500** fell 0.77% to 7,683.69 on Monday, and the Nasdaq dropped 0.92% to 26,820.38. That wiped out Friday's gains.
items.why: Trump rejected Iran's seven-day ceasefire plan, which pushed oil back up and revived inflation fears.

items.detail: The **10-year Treasury yield** hit **5.27%** on Monday, a new 19-year high, after Friday's pause. This week's PCE and jobs reports are next.
items.why: Higher oil raised the odds of an October Fed hike to 68%, up from 64% on Friday.

items.detail: The **MSCI Emerging Markets** gauge fell as much as 0.8% on Monday to a one-week low. Korea's Kospi dropped **2.6%** as it reopened after the holiday.
items.why: Trump's rejection of Iran's Hormuz offer lifted oil and global bond yields, which hurts oil-importing emerging markets most.

items.detail: India's **Nifty 50** fell 1.56% to **22,780** on Monday and slipped about 0.8% more early Tuesday to around 22,605.
items.why: Brent near $107 and a rupee weaker than 96 per dollar pushed foreign selling to ₹20,695 crore this month.

items.detail: The US **Russell 2000** fell **0.69%** to about 2,821 on Monday, reversing Friday's small gain.
items.why: A 10-year yield above 5.2% raises borrowing costs for debt-heavy small companies.

items.detail: **Bitcoin** slid to about **$83,000** on Monday, down roughly 1.8% in 24 hours, and dropped further below its weekend range.
items.why: Trump's snub of Iran's offer lifted oil, yields and the dollar, which weighed on assets that pay no yield.

items.detail: **Ether** fell about 1% on Monday to around **$2,646**, back at last Thursday's low after a brief weekend pause.
items.why: Rising bond yields and slower spot ETF inflows left no buyers to absorb profit-taking.

items.detail: **Solana** held near **$122.68** on Monday and beat BTC and ETH as its Alpenglow speed upgrade began rolling out.
items.why: US spot Solana ETFs took in a record $188 million last week, their best week since launch.

items.detail: **Spot gold** fell as much as 4% on Monday to **$4,111 an ounce**, its lowest since August 5, then held near $4,167 on Tuesday.
items.why: The oil spike raised Fed hike bets and pushed yields and the dollar up, making gold less attractive.

crossCuttingTheme: Trump's rejection of Iran's Hormuz ceasefire plan sent oil back up, pushing the 10-year to a 19-year high and raising October hike odds, which hit stocks, emerging markets, crypto and gold together.
